tires.evidence: City of Houston Recycling Centers page (fetched 2026-11-21): Accepted Materials: “Tires – residents may bring up to 5 (five) tires without rims.” (Westpark Center is the center listed with these accepted materials.)

paint.evidence: Latex only — City of Houston Recycling Centers page (fetched 2026-11-21): Accepted Materials: “B.O.P.A. – batteries, Oil, Latex Paint and Antifreeze.” Non-accepted items: “Oil Based Paint”.

e_waste.evidence: City of Houston Electronics & Recycling page (fetched 2026-11-21): “WESTPARK CONSUMER RECYCLING CENTER 5900 Westpark, Houston, TX 77057 Accepts residential electronics at no additional charge.” Accepted materials include computers, laptops, monitors, printers, “TVs (CRT TV's up to 36")”, cell phones.

batteries.evidence: City of Houston Recycling Centers page (fetched 2026-11-21): Accepted Materials: “B.O.P.A. – batteries, Oil, Latex Paint and Antifreeze.” City of Houston Electronics & Recycling page (fetched 2026-11-21): Non Acceptable Materials include “Household Alkaline Batteries (AA, AAA, C, D, 9V)”.

household_chemicals.evidence: City of Houston Recycling Centers page (fetched 2026-11-21): Non-accepted items: “Hazardous materials: Chemicals, oil, fuel, etc.”; “Household Hazardous Waste (HHW) Chemicals”.

quantity_limits.evidence: City of Houston Recycling Centers page (fetched 2026-11-21): “Residents may use the facilities up to four (4) times per month (once per week).”; “residents may bring up to 5 (five) tires without rims.”

accepts_text: Residential electronics (computers, laptops, monitors, printers, TVs including CRT TVs up to 36 in., cell phones, routers, cables, UPS units, copiers, fax machines, toner and ink cartridges); tires (up to 5, without rims); B.O.P.A. — batteries, oil, latex paint and antifreeze; scrap metal; recyclables (paper, cardboard, cartons, cans, glass, plastics #1–5 and #7). Not accepted: household hazardous waste chemicals, oil-based paint, heavy trash, garbage, alkaline household batteries in the electronics program
fees: Residential electronics accepted at no additional charge (other fees not stated)
notes: City of Houston Solid Waste Management Department. Proof of address: a current Texas-issued ID (driver's license, DPS ID, License to Carry or Consulate ID) or a current City of Houston utility bill or lease; for recycling only a current Texas-issued ID is sufficient. Residents may use the recycling centers up to 4 times per month (once per week); arrive at least 15–30 minutes before closing. The Recycling Centers page lists B.O.P.A. (batteries, oil, latex paint and antifreeze) as accepted but also lists “Hazardous materials: Chemicals, oil, fuel” as not accepted, so call 311 before bringing motor oil. Electronics details: https://www.houstontx.gov/solidwaste/ewaste.

name: Ellington/Clear Lake Neighborhood Recycling Center

id_required.evidence: City of Houston Recycling Centers page (fetched 2026-11-21): “To use any City of Houston Residential Drop‑Off Centers, Recycling Centers, or Environmental Service Centers, residents must present one of the following: A current Texas-issued ID … OR A current City of Houston utility bill or lease/rental agreement”; “For recycling only: A current Texas-issued ID is sufficient.”

e_waste.evidence: Monthly event only — City of Houston Electronics & Recycling page (fetched 2026-11-21): “The monthly Saturday electronics recycling events will be held 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. at the: … Ellington/Clear Lake Neighborhood Recycling Center When: 2nd Saturday of each month Time: 9:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m.”

quantity_limits.evidence: City of Houston Recycling Centers page (fetched 2026-11-21): “Residents may use the facilities up to four (4) times per month (once per week).”

hours: Open 7 days a week 8am–8pm; electronics recycling event 2nd Saturday of each month 9am–3pm
accepts_text: Recyclables (paper, cardboard, cartons, cans, glass, plastics #1–5 and #7); residential electronics at the monthly 2nd-Saturday event (computers, laptops, monitors, printers, TVs including CRT TVs up to 36 in., cell phones, routers, cables, UPS units, copiers, fax machines, toner and ink cartridges). Not accepted at the electronics event: vacuum cleaners, CRT TVs over 36 in., radios, game consoles, microwaves and other appliances, fluorescent bulbs, smoke detectors, alkaline batteries, paint cans
notes: City of Houston Solid Waste Management Department. Proof of address: a current Texas-issued ID (driver's license, DPS ID, License to Carry or Consulate ID) or a current City of Houston utility bill or lease; for recycling only a current Texas-issued ID is sufficient. Residents may use the recycling centers up to 4 times per month (once per week); arrive at least 15–30 minutes before closing. Electronics are taken only at the monthly 2nd-Saturday event (details: https://www.houstontx.gov/solidwaste/ewaste). The Recycling Centers page also lists tires and B.O.P.A. in a general accepted-materials list without naming sites, so call 311 before bringing tires, oil or batteries.
